title: Operating system installation and BIOS/UEFI

spans.text: Installation or formatting can erase files. Get the device owner’s approval, copy important files elsewhere, and verify that the backup opens. Prepare BitLocker/FileVault recovery keys, license details, Wi-Fi access, and official drivers. Plug in a laptop. Stop if you cannot identify the disk and its partitions.

Download Microsoft’s Media Creation Tool from the official Windows 11 page. Select a blank USB drive of at least 8 GB; creation erases it. Restart, open the manufacturer-specific Boot Menu (F12, F9, Esc, etc.), and choose the USB. Set language and keyboard. At disk selection, confirm model and capacity; erasing the wrong partition can destroy other data.

Finish setup and run Windows Update. Get missing drivers only from the computer maker’s official site; check Device Manager for yellow warnings. Test internet, sound, camera, Wi-Fi, display, and sleep. Confirm activation and backup status. Never put a recovery key in a support ticket.

Download an ISO from Ubuntu or another distribution’s official site; verify SHA-256 if offered. Create USB media using official instructions, boot from it, and try Try Ubuntu first to check Wi-Fi, sound, and display. Choose Install Ubuntu and set language, keyboard, and network. Erase disk can remove the entire selected disk. Choose dual boot or manual partitioning only when you understand the plan.
Apply updates, review optional driver offers, restart, and test hardware. Plan the backup, boot order, and encryption choice before installation.

Back up a Mac with Time Machine or an approved method. On Apple silicon, shut down, hold the power button until startup options appear, and choose Options. On an Intel Mac, hold Command-R while starting. Connect to the internet in Recovery and choose Reinstall macOS. Erase with Disk Utility only if needed; confirm the correct disk and APFS. Activation Lock may require the Apple Account.

BIOS/UEFI is motherboard firmware that checks hardware at startup. Del, F2, F10, or Esc varies by model; Windows Advanced startup may also open UEFI settings. Boot order selects the USB startup device. VT-x/AMD-V may be needed for VMs. Do not change Secure Boot, TPM, SATA, or boot settings without a reason; record the old value first. A wrong change can trigger BitLocker recovery or prevent startup.
